introduction.md: Meet Fastmash: fast command-line statistics for text and quoted CSV, portable results, record selection, table health and dataset comparison.
install.md: Install published Linux and WSL2 versions of Fastmash, or verify an Apple Silicon macOS development archive from native CI.
quick-start.md: Learn Fastmash through practical examples of statistics, grouping, quoted CSV, result names, weighted means and complete-record selection.
guide/migrating.md: Move a GNU datamash workflow to Fastmash: what stays the same, how to switch safely and which compatibility differences to check.
comparison.md: Compare Fastmash with GNU datamash, Miller, qsv and csvtk, including command languages, input formats, statistics and supported platforms.
guide/index.md: Find Fastmash's user guide to fields, operations, grouping, text transformations, numeric output, locales and error handling.
guide/input.md: Choose Fastmash fields by number, range or header name, and configure separators, records, comments, whitespace or explicit quoted CSV.
guide/operations.md: Look up Fastmash statistics and aggregates, including weighted means, quantiles, dispersion, normality tests, paired statistics and text operations.
guide/grouping.md: Group and sort delimited data with Fastmash: grouping keys, sorted input, headers, crosstabs and the memory used by sorting.
guide/modes.md: Use Fastmash per-row and table modes, from field selection and transposition to complete-record ranking, table health and dataset comparison.
guide/output.md: Understand Fastmash's number parsing, portable arithmetic, output formatting, locale rules and handling of missing or special numeric values.
guide/errors.md: Understand Fastmash diagnostics, exit statuses, explicit refusals and resource requirements when a command cannot complete.
guide/differences.md: Check the documented differences between Fastmash and GNU datamash 1.9, including numerical results, locales, errors and unsupported cases.
requirements.md: Check Fastmash's released Linux requirements and native Apple Silicon macOS development scope, sorting and source-build requirements.
benchmarks/index.md: See Fastmash 0.1.0 benchmark results against GNU datamash on real and synthetic data, including speed improvements and remaining slower cases.
benchmarks/method.md: Read how Fastmash benchmarks are measured, checked and compared, with workload definitions, hardware details and complete result tables.
faq.md: Answers to common Fastmash questions about datamash compatibility, performance, supported systems, input formats and portable results.
roadmap.md: See Fastmash's planned Apple Silicon macOS support for 0.2.0 and further performance, sorting, locale, packaging and table-workflow improvements.
contributing/index.md: Help improve Fastmash by reporting compatibility differences, testing real data, sharing benchmarks, improving documentation or contributing code.
contributing/architecture.md: Explore Fastmash's Rust crates, command pipeline, numeric boundaries, grouping and sorting design, and the principles behind them.
contributing/testing.md: Build and test Fastmash with formatting, linting, unit tests, the regression corpus and checks for numerical or performance changes.
contributing/glossary.md: Understand the shared vocabulary used in Fastmash's code and documentation, including commands, operations, fields, groups and sort routes.
adr/index.md: Browse the design decisions behind Fastmash's command language, Rust implementation, portable arithmetic, sorting and locale tables.
adr/0001-gnu-command-language.md: Why Fastmash independently implements the GNU datamash command language so existing commands and workflows can be reused.
adr/0002-rust-without-c-numerics.md: Why Fastmash uses Rust throughout, including software arithmetic, instead of retaining numerical kernels written in C.
adr/0003-portable-results.md: Why Fastmash targets identical numerical results across supported machines instead of reproducing each host's C math library.
adr/0004-refuse-rather-than-guess.md: Why Fastmash explicitly refuses unsupported cases with exit status 77 rather than guessing at results it cannot establish.
adr/0005-growable-checked-storage.md: Why Fastmash uses growable, checked storage instead of fixed record limits, and how memory use and disk spilling affect commands.
adr/0006-supervised-external-sort.md: Why Fastmash supervises external sort processes and how the supervisor manages their lifetime, temporary files and cleanup.
adr/0007-linux-first.md: Why Fastmash initially supports Linux x86-64 and WSL2, and what limits its current platform coverage.
adr/0008-hash-grouping-with-restart.md: Why Fastmash groups eligible sorted jobs by hash and restarts through sorting when needed to preserve the expected output.
adr/0009-built-in-locale-tables.md: Why Fastmash carries built-in locale rules instead of relying on locale data installed on the host machine.
adr/0010-native-apple-silicon.md: Why native Apple Silicon support requires macOS 15 and 26 command checks and installation of the same archive on both baselines.
about.md: Learn about Fastmash's creator, its independent relationship to GNU datamash, the project's motivation and where to get in touch.
guide/csv-and-result-names.md: Read and write strict quoted CSV in Fastmash, choose formats independently and give calculated output columns stable result names.
guide/weighted-mean.md: Calculate weighted means with finite nonnegative contribution weights, text or CSV, grouping, headers and checked numerical limits.
guide/top-n-records.md: Select the highest or lowest complete records with stable input-order ties, explicit headers, text or CSV and a cutoff per group.
guide/dataset-comparison.md: Compare numerical summaries from two datasets, align complete keys and independently named headers, and rank absolute or percentage changes.
guide/table-health.md: Inspect Fastmash table health, review inferred findings, validate supplied type, presence and width rules, and read versioned TSV reports.
guide/terminal-color.md: Control Fastmash terminal styling for help, failure prefixes and readable health reports, with automatic detection and color suppression.
